newsitem.title: TAIWAN: CHINA STEEL UP DESPITE GOVT AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: CHINA STEEL UP DESPITE GOVT AUCTION.

text.p: Taiwan steel giant China Steel rose in late Tuesday trade on sound outlook, despite government auctioning of 182 million state-owned shares of the firm, brokers said.
* On Monday, the government auctioned off some 92.79 million shares in China Steel at a total value of T$2.89 billion. It will continue the auction in afternoon.
* With 40 minutes left at 0320 GMT, China Steel was up 30 cents or 0.96 percent to T$31.8. Turnover was 48 million shares, the market's third biggest so far on Tuesday.
* "This is a vote of confidence for China Steel as institutional investors have shown great interest in the company," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
* "One foreign institution reportedly plans to buy off most of the government auction this week on China Steel," Hung said.
* China Steel was comparatively low-priced, with a price-earnings ratio of some 14, much lower than the market's average of 36, Hung said.
* China Steel said in June its 1997/1998 earnings per share will reach T$2.25 -- a record for the firm -- due to completion of its expansion and international steel price hikes.
